findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. That covers 'what' and 'why' in a few sentences.
findings.source: header, first lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The title and heading are about firstmate, a different project, not about Athena. A newcomer who came to the Athena site can't tell from the heading that this is Athena's homepage, and has to reach the third paragraph to learn that the page is a demonstration study.
findings.source: <title> and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The first section after the navigation is a visible failure. It was meant to show the models, verdict and cost, which the lede promises, and it shows none of them. That weakens the evidence for Athena's main selling point, and the raw error text means nothing to a newcomer.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link is aimed at the site's owner, but it sits near the top of the newcomer's view with no explanation. A first-time reader may think they are being asked to make decisions.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: clone, prerequisites, setup, then a first command, with a note that it acts on the current repository and waits for Enter. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps: prerequisites list and "Install Athena from the checkout: ./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The page says cargo builds Athena, but the prerequisites list does not include Rust or cargo, and it does not say whether setup.sh installs them. A newcomer may not know whether they need a Rust toolchain.
findings.source: Next steps: "a C linker (cc), which cargo needs to build Athena"

findings.text: The page never names the models or says roughly what a run costs. The only hint is "Claude Code" in the prerequisites. A newcomer can't judge cost or vendor lock-in before installing.
findings.source: header lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine of firstmate. It shows how rigorously Athena traces claims, but a newcomer who wants to learn about Athena has to scroll through it, and the only short route to Athena is the 'Next step' link in the header.
findings.source: Start here through Claims and sources (12 transition cards, 40+ glossary entries, 45 claims)

findings.text: Several glossary entries say plainly what the source does not define, which builds trust in the tracing. But they leave words like endpoint, wake and captain call without a usable definition.
findings.source: Glossary, e.g. endpoint: "The firstmate source does not define an endpoint. The cited text shows only that..."
